ideation.objective: Document and stabilize a desktop-first AI clipping platform that turns long-form and livestream content into publishable short-form clips for individual creators and organization teams.
ideation.core_outcome: A reliable end-to-end workflow from media ingestion through AI detection, editing, collaboration, and distribution across desktop and web interfaces.
target_audience: Individual creators producing short-form clips from long videos and streams
Organization owners and team members managing shared content, assets, and campaigns
Internal admins and moderators operating support, policy, and growth workflows
core_experience: Ingest media from VOD/live/local sources and generate transcripts and candidate clips with AI.
Refine output in a professional editing experience (timeline/OpenCut) with local desktop performance.
Coordinate publishing, messaging, billing, and organization workflows through authenticated backend APIs.
success_signals: Clip detection, transcription, and editing workflows complete consistently without manual recovery.
Organization collaboration surfaces (shared clips, messaging, creator/campaign tools) are actively used without access-control regressions.
Release pipeline continuously ships signed desktop artifacts and fresh server/landing deployments.
Billing and credit ledgers remain accurate across subscription, promo, and pay-per-use paths.
risks: Heavy dependence on third-party services (OpenRouter, Whisper API, Stripe, social APIs) increases failure modes and operational variance.
Very broad backend API and controller surface raises regression risk when domain behavior changes.
Sparse automated tests (few backend tests, no evident client/landing test suite) weakens release confidence.
Cross-platform binary/signing/notarization complexity in the Tauri release flow can block shipping if tooling drifts.
assumptions: Desktop (Tauri) remains the primary production surface while landing provides marketing plus authenticated web dashboard/admin entry points.
Credit/subscription economics remain tied to AI/media processing usage rather than unlimited free operations.
Organization workflows (members, assets, messaging, shared clips, campaigns) remain core product differentiators.
open_questions: Which documented security hardening tasks are mandatory before the next production release gate?
What SLO/error budgets are acceptable for AI-dependent workflows given third-party API dependencies?
How should testing investment be prioritized across server, desktop client, and landing/admin surfaces?

blocks.title: Product Surface and User Workflows
blocks.rationale: The repository contains multiple user-facing surfaces with overlapping capabilities and role-specific flows that need precise documentation.

topics.title: Desktop Creator Workflow
topics.why_it_matters: The desktop client is the primary runtime for ingestion, AI clip generation, and editing, so its user journey defines core product value.
research_questions: What is the canonical step-by-step workflow from project creation to exported clip in the desktop app?
Which flows are gated by tier or feature flags and how are those gates enforced client-side and server-side?

topics.title: Organization Collaboration Workflow
topics.why_it_matters: Organization features span membership, assets, messaging, and campaigns and significantly expand product scope beyond solo creators.
research_questions: How do owner/admin/member permissions map across organization routes and APIs?
What are the key collaboration loops between shared clips, messaging, and creator/campaign management?

topics.title: Landing and Web Dashboard Scope
topics.why_it_matters: The landing app includes both marketing and authenticated dashboard/admin routes, which affects product boundary and ownership.
research_questions: Which capabilities are marketing-only versus authenticated dashboard functionality in the landing codebase?
How much overlap exists between desktop and landing-admin capabilities, and where should source-of-truth UX live?

blocks.title: AI and Media Processing Pipeline
blocks.rationale: AI/media orchestration is the core differentiator and combines transcription, chunking, multimodel detection, and editing/export runtime concerns.

topics.title: Ingest, Transcription, and Detection Pipeline
topics.why_it_matters: Clip generation reliability depends on correct sequencing of upload/chunk/transcription/detection and error handling across services.
research_questions: Where are chunk boundaries, retries, and timeout policies defined for transcription and detection?
How are credits, jobs, and progress events tied into each pipeline phase?

topics.title: Multimodel Consensus and Fallback Logic
topics.why_it_matters: Multimodel orchestration introduces additional cost and complexity and must be understood for quality/cost tradeoffs.
research_questions: How are model outputs merged, validated, and downgraded to fallback behavior when decider steps fail?
What token/cost telemetry is captured per model and how is it surfaced?

topics.title: Desktop Editing and Export Runtime
topics.why_it_matters: Professional editing UX and export output quality are directly tied to local storage, ffmpeg sidecars, and editor-state persistence.
research_questions: How do OpenCut storage adapters and local SQLite schemas coordinate with main project data?
Which export paths rely on sidecars versus in-process media operations?

blocks.title: Backend Domain and Platform Services
blocks.rationale: The Phoenix backend contains extensive domain modules and API endpoints that govern product behavior, access control, and monetization.

topics.title: API Surface and Domain Boundaries
topics.why_it_matters: Large controller and route surfaces increase coupling and change risk; documenting boundaries supports safer evolution.
research_questions: Which contexts are truly bounded domains versus convenience aggregations?
Where do route groups and auth pipelines imply hidden coupling between features?

topics.title: Realtime Messaging and Progress Channels
topics.why_it_matters: Realtime channels back both team messaging and long-running AI workflow feedback, so channel auth and event design are critical.
research_questions: How are websocket topics authorized and what ownership guarantees are enforced per channel?
What event contracts must stay stable across desktop and landing clients?

topics.title: Billing, Credits, and Subscription Logic
topics.why_it_matters: Credit and subscription logic controls access and revenue, and spans personal plus organization billing flows.
research_questions: How do personal and organization subscription states interact with feature gates and credit deduction?
Which Stripe and crypto paths are production-critical and where are idempotency guarantees enforced?

blocks.title: Release, Deployment, and Runtime Operations
blocks.rationale: Shipping depends on a complex release pipeline spanning signed desktop artifacts and Fly.io deployments for backend and landing.

topics.title: Tauri Multi-Platform Release Automation
topics.why_it_matters: Desktop distribution requires signing, notarization, updater artifacts, and architecture-specific binaries in one workflow.
research_questions: Which steps in the GitHub release workflow are the highest failure-risk for macOS and Windows artifacts?
How are sidecar binary provenance, signing, and updater signatures validated end-to-end?

topics.title: Server and Landing Deploy Topology
topics.why_it_matters: Runtime behavior and incident response depend on how Phoenix and landing apps are deployed and scaled.
research_questions: How are Fly.io app configs, health checks, and scaling defaults aligned with production traffic expectations?
Which deployment steps are tightly coupled to the release branch workflow?

topics.title: Runtime Config and Secret Contracts
topics.why_it_matters: Many critical integrations are environment-driven; missing or misconfigured secrets can silently degrade key features.
research_questions: Which env vars are hard requirements for production-safe behavior versus optional enhancements?
How can startup validation and observability reduce misconfiguration time-to-detect?

blocks.title: Quality, Security, and Readiness
blocks.rationale: Current test coverage and hardening posture determine the risk profile for continued feature velocity and production stability.

topics.title: Automated Test Strategy Gaps
topics.why_it_matters: The codebase appears to have minimal automated tests relative to scope, increasing regression probability.
research_questions: What is the minimum viable cross-surface test pyramid to protect core clipping and billing workflows?
Which modules should be prioritized first for deterministic integration tests?

topics.title: Security Hardening Hotspots
topics.why_it_matters: Authentication, payment, and channel authorization paths include known high-impact hotspots that warrant formal hardening.
research_questions: Which auth/payment/socket flows need immediate remediation before broader scale-out?
How should security checks be codified as release gates rather than one-off audits?

topics.title: Operational Observability and Maintenance
topics.why_it_matters: Sustainable operations require actionable logs, monitoring, and maintenance workflows across AI jobs and release systems.
research_questions: Where are critical metrics/events emitted today and where are visibility gaps?
What maintenance burdens (binary/toolchain drift, migration safety, doc drift) should be scheduled proactively?
